killed_pre_attempt.what: A FIRST set of four machines was launched at 18:18:19-18:18:30Z and TERMINATED BY THIS DESK ~70 seconds later, before relaunching as the machines above.
killed_pre_attempt.why: They were issued WITHOUT `--rec-slots 8`, so they took spot_run.sh's default `REC_SLOTS=1`. That is a defect, not a preference, for two independent reasons: (1) it moves the ACQUISITION CONFIG in the same wave that moves the tested id set, which the charter forbids precisely so a surprising reading cannot be blamed on two changes at once; (2) this wave exists to buy ONE behavioral reading (the GH #241 `.type` premise), the reading runs on behav-dump timelines produced from RECORDED games, and at rec_slots=1 of 16 slots the recorded corpus is ~1/8 of the W39-W50 standard -- the likely outcome is `DOMAIN-NOT-REACHED`, which the ruling explicitly forbids reading as 'tested, `.type` is not a string'. A wave that cannot answer its own question is worth less than the $0.06 saved by not relaunching it.
killed_pre_attempt.why_fresh_seeds_for_the_relaunch: The relaunch uses FOUR DIFFERENT seeds (6421/6487/6553/6619), not the four the dead machines held. ~70s is almost certainly too short to produce even a warm-up game, but 'almost certainly zero' is an ASSUMPTION, and `recover_verdict.py` pools by the `s<SEED>` stamp ACROSS runs -- so a single stray game under a dead prefix would pool into this wave's reading with nobody raising a hand. Fresh seeds remove the assumption instead of relying on it. The four burned seeds are now spent and must not be re-offered; `seed_roster_index.py --build` will only learn that if those prefixes hold games, so treat 6211/6277/6343/6409 as USED by hand.
